## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sunikkhittavimānavatthu* (Vv 85), rendered as "Sunikkhitta’s Mansion," is a verse narrative within the *Vimānavatthu* of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. In the text, the arahant Mahāmoggallāna encounters a powerful deva and inquires about the specific meritorious actions that led to the attainment of such an exalted divine state [SuttaCentral]. The work exemplifies the core didactic theme of the collection, illustrating the direct karmic fruits of meritorious acts through heavenly rebirth [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records four translations of the text in four languages [SuttaCentral].
Textual reuse analysis demonstrates that the poem relies heavily on stock formulas common to the *Vimānavatthu* [DharmaNexus]. The commentary, *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, preserves and explains the text across 73 shared passages encompassing segments §1.1–5.4 [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus computes 174 matching passages with 33 other Pali texts, showing extensive formulaic sharing; notably, segments §2.4–5.4 closely mirror portions of the *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), the *Tiladakkhiṇavimānavatthu* (Vv 10), and the *Kakkaṭakarasadāyakavimānavatthu* (Vv 54), the latter exhibiting an alignment over §0.4–5.4 [DharmaNexus]. Beyond the Pali tradition, DharmaNexus generates machine alignments with the Sanskrit *Suvarṇavarṇāvadāna* as well as the Chinese translations of the *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra* (T 7) and *Ekottarika-āgama* (T 125), though these represent computational text reuse rather than established direct parallels [DharmaNexus].
